title: The Thirsty Moonflower
attribution: Inspired by Aesop’s The Crow and the Pitcher

pages.heading: Before the Dark
pages.text: Artus and Pip reached the moon garden. The sun was low. But the great white flower was shut. “That is odd,” said Artus.
pages.alt: Artus and Pip in the moon garden story, illustration 1.

pages.text: Each night, the flower lit the path home. Without its glow, the tiny moths would get lost. “We must wake it!” cried Pip.
pages.alt: Artus and Pip in the moon garden story, illustration 2.

pages.text: Artus felt the dry soil. “It needs water.” He took his little wooden cup. Pip peered inside. “Not one drop. Oh dear!”
pages.alt: Artus and Pip in the moon garden story, illustration 3.

pages.text: They ran to the stream. Its bed was dry. Pip poked a stone. “Even the fish have packed up!” Then they heard a caw.
pages.alt: Artus and Pip in the moon garden story, illustration 4.

pages.text: A crow flapped down. “There is water by the old tower.” “Show us!” said Artus. The crow flew up the hill.
pages.alt: Artus and Pip in the moon garden story, illustration 5.

pages.text: The path grew steep. Artus stopped at a narrow ledge. “Stay close,” he said. Pip pressed against his boot. “I am right here.”
pages.alt: Artus and Pip in the moon garden story, illustration 6.

pages.text: By the tower stood a tall stone jar. Water shone far down inside. “Found it!” cried Pip. “Now we just need to reach it.”
pages.alt: Artus and Pip in the moon garden story, illustration 7.

pages.text: Pip stretched one paw. He stretched his neck. “Just a bit more…” His nose touched cold stone. The water was still too far away.
pages.alt: Artus and Pip in the moon garden story, illustration 8.

pages.text: Artus pushed the jar. Pip pushed too. They huffed. They puffed. The jar did not move. “It is heavier than both of us!”
pages.alt: Artus and Pip in the moon garden story, illustration 9.

pages.text: Artus raised his staff. A soft light shone inside the jar. “I can light the water,” he sighed. “But I cannot lift it.”
pages.alt: Artus and Pip in the moon garden story, illustration 10.

pages.text: Pip sat down with a thump. “My paws are too short.” Artus sat beside him. “Then we need a new idea.” They listened.
pages.alt: Artus and Pip in the moon garden story, illustration 11.

pages.text: The crow picked up a pebble. It hopped to the jar. Plop! A ring spread over the water. Pip leaned close. “Do that again!”
pages.alt: Artus and Pip in the moon garden story, illustration 12.

pages.heading: One Small Stone
pages.text: Plop went another stone. The water crept up the wall. Artus blinked. “The stones take up space!” Pip grinned. “Then let us find more!”
pages.alt: Artus and Pip in the moon garden story, illustration 13.

pages.text: They dropped in three small stones. The water rose a little more. “It works!” said Pip. He gave a hop. “Little stones can help!”
pages.alt: Artus and Pip in the moon garden story, illustration 14.

pages.text: Artus found smooth stones by the path. Pip swept leaves aside with his tail. A whole pile lay underneath. “Treasure!” he cried.
pages.alt: Artus and Pip in the moon garden story, illustration 15.

pages.text: Pip dropped in some leaves. “These are light!” The leaves floated. The water stayed low. “Stones,” said Artus, with a smile.
pages.alt: Artus and Pip in the moon garden story, illustration 16.

pages.text: Artus lifted a big rock. It would not fit through the neck. Pip nudged his hand. “Small ones, remember?” “Right,” said Artus. “Small ones.”
pages.alt: Artus and Pip in the moon garden story, illustration 17.

pages.text: Back and forth they went. Pick up. Carry. Drop. The tower filled with tiny plops. Far below, the garden grew dark. The flower still had no light.
pages.alt: Artus and Pip in the moon garden story, illustration 18.

pages.text: Artus rubbed his tired hands. Pip leaned against him. “My turn to carry,” said Pip. “Our turn,” said Artus. They picked up one more stone.
pages.alt: Artus and Pip in the moon garden story, illustration 19.

pages.text: The crow gave a loud call. Two more crows swooped down. Each brought a pebble. Pip looked up. “Now that is a good flock of ideas!”
pages.alt: Artus and Pip in the moon garden story, illustration 20.

pages.text: One stone. Two stones. Three. The water rose past an old mark. Pip held his breath. Artus reached for his cup. “Nearly there…”
pages.alt: Artus and Pip in the moon garden story, illustration 21.

pages.text: At last, Artus dipped the cup. It came up full. The crow took a sip from the jar. Pip beamed. “Water for everyone!”
pages.alt: Artus and Pip in the moon garden story, illustration 22.

pages.text: Water splashed on Artus’s boot. “Careful!” said Pip. Artus slowed down. Step by step, they took the water home.
pages.alt: Artus and Pip in the moon garden story, illustration 23.

pages.text: Artus poured the water onto the roots. The flower lifted its head. One petal opened. Then another. Silver light spilled over the path. Pip gasped.
pages.alt: Artus and Pip in the moon garden story, illustration 24.

pages.text: The moths followed the glow all the way home. Pip curled beside Artus. “We did it.” Artus smiled. “Yes, we did.” One small stone lay between them.
pages.alt: Artus and Pip in the moon garden story, illustration 25.
